Rule.name: Islamic New Year
Rule.comment: Hijri New Year (Ra's as-Sanah al-Hijriyyah). The first day of Muharram, the opening month of the Islamic lunar calendar. Marks the anniversary of the Prophet Muhammad's migration (Hijra) from Mecca to Medina in 622 CE, from which the Hijri calendar era is dated. A public holiday in many Muslim-majority countries. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'islamic-new-year'.

Rule.name: Day of Ashura
Rule.comment: Yawm Ashura. Falls on the tenth day of Muharram. For Sunni Muslims it is a recommended fast day commemorating Moses' fast in gratitude for the Israelites' deliverance. For Shia Muslims it is a major day of mourning commemorating the martyrdom of Hussein ibn Ali at the Battle of Karbala (61 AH / 680 CE). Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'day-of-ashura'.

Rule.name: Mawlid al-Nabi
Rule.comment: The Prophet's Birthday (Mawlid an-Nabawi). Observed on the 12th of Rabi al-Awwal in Sunni tradition and the 17th in Shia tradition. Commemorates the birth of the Prophet Muhammad. A public holiday in many Muslim-majority countries; not observed by some denominations that consider it an innovation (bid'ah). Algorithm implementations should document which convention (Sunni 12th or Shia 17th) they apply. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'mawlid-al-nabi'.

Rule.name: Ramadan
Rule.comment: The ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of fasting (sawm), prayer, reflection, and community. The fast runs from dawn (Fajr) to sunset (Maghrib) each day. The month lasts 29 or 30 days depending on the lunar cycle. The durationDays value of 30 represents the maximum span; implementations may return either 29 or 30 depending on the year. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'ramadan-start'.

Rule.name: Eid al-Fitr
Rule.comment: The Festival of Breaking the Fast. Celebrated on the first day of Shawwal, the month following Ramadan. One of the two major Islamic festivals (Eid). Observed with communal prayers, feasting, giving of Zakat al-Fitr (charitable donations), and the exchange of gifts. A public holiday in most Muslim-majority countries, typically lasting three days. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'eid-al-fitr'.

Rule.name: Eid al-Adha
Rule.comment: The Festival of Sacrifice (Feast of the Sacrifice). Celebrated on the tenth day of Dhul Hijja, the final month of the Islamic calendar, coinciding with the completion of the Hajj pilgrimage. Commemorates Ibrahim's (Abraham's) willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to God. Observed with communal prayers, the ritual slaughter of livestock, and distribution of meat to family, friends, and those in need. A public holiday in most Muslim-majority countries, typically lasting four days. Requires a custom INotableDateAlgorithm registered under the key 'eid-al-adha'.
